claim: A backup plan that points to a deleted backup vault makes backup creation fail, so you update plans to point to new vaults when you delete a vault.
question: What happens to a backup plan whose target vault is deleted?

values.display: points to a deleted backup vault
cause the backup creation to fail

evidence.quote: When you delete a backup vault, update your backup plans to point to new backup vaults. A backup plan that points to a deleted backup vault will cause the backup creation to fail.

claim: In the API, a vault lock is created in governance mode when you leave out ChangeableForDays; if you include that parameter, the lock is created in compliance mode.
question: How does the Vault Lock API choose between governance mode and compliance mode?

values.display: do not include ChangeableForDays
created in compliance mode

evidence.quote: If you wish to create a vault lock in governance mode, do not include `ChangeableForDays`. If this parameter is included, the vault lock will be created in compliance mode.

claim: With a vault lock minimum and maximum retention, new backup and copy jobs that do not conform fail, while recovery points already in the vault keep their previous lifecycle settings.
question: What happens to jobs and existing recovery points when Vault Lock sets minimum and maximum retention?

values.display: will fail if they do not conform
not apply to recovery points that are already in the vault

qualifiers.scope: Vault Lock min and max retention

evidence.quote: New backup and copy jobs created in the vault will fail if they do not conform to the retention periods you set; these periods will not apply to recovery points that are already in the vault. Recovery points that were present in the vault prior to the vault lock being enabled will follow their previous lifecycle settings.

claim: If you do not set a maximum (or minimum) retention period, Vault Lock does not enforce one.
question: Does Vault Lock enforce a retention range if you do not set one?

values.display: will not enforce a maximum retention period
will not enforce a minimum retention period

qualifiers.scope: Vault Lock min and max retention

evidence.quote: If not specified, AWS Backup Vault Lock will not enforce a maximum retention period. If specified, backup and copy jobs to this vault with lifecycle retention periods longer than the maximum retention period will fail.

If not specified, AWS Backup Vault Lock will not enforce a minimum retention period. If specified, backup and copy jobs to this vault with lifecycle retention periods shorter than the minimum retention period will fail.

claim: Vault Lock gives a write-once, read-many (WORM) configuration for all backups in a vault and an additional layer of defense against inadvertent or malicious deletion.
question: What does AWS Backup Vault Lock give you?

values.display: WORM (write-once, read-many) configuration
inadvertent or malicious deletions

evidence.quote: WORM (write-once, read-many) configuration for all the backups you store and create in a backup vault.
An additional layer of defense that protects backups (recovery points) in your backup vaults from inadvertent or malicious deletions.

claim: Vault Lock enforces backup lifecycle retention periods, which prevents early deletions by privileged users, including the AWS account root user.
question: Does Vault Lock stop privileged users, including root, from deleting backups early?

values.display: prevent early deletions by privileged users
AWS account root user

evidence.quote: Enforcement of backup lifecycle retention periods, which prevent early deletions by privileged users (including the AWS account root user), and help meet your organization’s data protection policies and procedures.

Standard AWS Backup storage charges apply

claim: Backups within a locked vault cannot be deleted until their lifecycle completes, which gives persistent costs if retention is set too long; a recovery point with retention set to Always is kept forever once the grace time expires.
question: Can you delete a backup in a locked vault before its lifecycle ends, and what is the cost risk?

values.display: cannot be deleted until their lifecycle completes
retained forever

qualifiers.condition: the grace time has expired for the Always example

evidence.quote: Backups within a locked vault cannot be deleted until their lifecycle completes, resulting in persistent costs if you are not careful. For example, ensure there are no recovery points with a retention period set to "Always"—once the grace time expires, these recovery points will be retained forever and cannot be altered or deleted.

claim: If you close an AWS account that contains a backup vault, AWS suspends the account for 90 days with backups intact, and if you do not reopen it in that time AWS deletes the vault contents even when Vault Lock was in place.
question: Does Vault Lock protect backups if the AWS account is closed?

values.display: suspend your account for 90 days
even if AWS Backup Vault Lock was in place

qualifiers.scope: closing an AWS account with a locked vault

evidence.quote: When you close an AWS account that contains a backup vault, AWS and AWS Backup suspend your account for 90 days with your backups intact. If you do not reopen your account during those 90 days, AWS deletes the contents of your backup vault, even if AWS Backup Vault Lock was in place.

claim: A logically air-gapped vault can be the primary backup destination in the same account for scheduled and on-demand jobs, which removes the need to keep separate copies in a standard vault and a logically air-gapped vault.
question: Can backups go straight into a logically air-gapped vault instead of being copied from a standard vault?

values.display: primary backup destination within the same account
separate copies in both a standard backup vault

evidence.quote: The logically air-gapped vault primary backup feature offers you the option to specify a logically air-gapped vault as a primary backup destination within the same account, for both scheduled and on-demand backup jobs. This eliminates the need to maintain separate copies in both a standard backup vault and a logically air-gapped vault, reducing costs and simplifying workflows while preserving the security benefits of logical air-gapping.

claim: To back up directly into a logically air-gapped vault, the vault must be in the same account and Region as your resources; you cannot create such backups directly cross-account or cross-Region.
question: Can a primary backup go directly to a logically air-gapped vault in another Region or account?

values.display: same AWS account and Region as your resources
cannot create backups directly cross-account or cross-Region

evidence.quote: Your logically air-gapped vault must be in the same AWS account and Region as your resources to use this feature. You cannot create backups directly cross-account or cross-Region.

claim: Resource types with full AWS Backup management, such as EFS, S3 and DynamoDB with advanced features, can back up directly to a logically air-gapped vault: no recovery point is created in the backup vault and no copy operation is required.
question: Which resource types back up directly to a logically air-gapped vault with no copy?

values.display: can back up directly to your logically air-gapped vault
no copy operation is required

qualifiers.scope: resource types supporting full AWS Backup management

evidence.quote: Some resource types, such as Amazon EFS, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB with AWS Backup advanced features etc., that support full AWS Backup management, can back up directly to your logically air-gapped vault. No recovery point is created in your backup vault, and no copy operation is required.

claim: Resources such as EBS, EC2, Aurora and FSx cannot back up directly to a logically air-gapped vault: AWS Backup creates a temporary recovery point in the backup vault and then automatically copies it to the logically air-gapped vault.
question: How do EBS, EC2, Aurora and FSx get backed up to a logically air-gapped vault as the primary target?

values.display: cannot back up directly to logically air-gapped vaults
temporary recovery point in your backup vault

qualifiers.scope: resource types not supporting full AWS Backup management

evidence.quote: Resources such as Amazon EBS/EC2, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon FSx cannot back up directly to logically air-gapped vaults. For these resource types, AWS Backup creates a temporary recovery point in your backup vault and then automatically copies it to your logically air-gapped vault.

claim: The logically air-gapped vault primary backup feature has no new pricing: you pay only for backups stored in logically air-gapped vaults and, for applicable resources, temporary snapshots at prevailing rates.
question: Does primary backup to a logically air-gapped vault add a charge?

values.display: no new pricing for this feature
temporary snapshots

evidence.quote: There is no new pricing for this feature. You are only charged for backups stored in logically air-gapped vaults and for temporary snapshots (during their retention period in the system) for applicable resources at prevailing rates.

claim: Multi-party approval is a capability from AWS Organizations that you can add to logically air-gapped vaults, to protect critical operations through a distributed approval process.

distributed approval process

claim: Multi-party approval helps protect critical resources and shorten the time to return to full operation after a disruption by malicious actors or malware, and helps you restore the contents of a logically air-gapped vault that may have been compromised.
question: What is multi-party approval used for in AWS Backup?

values.display: minimize the time to return to full operation
may have been compromised

evidence.quote: Multi-party approval is designed to help protect critical resources and to minimize the time to return to full operation, such as a disruption caused by malicious actors or malware events. This setup can help you restore the contents of a logically air-gapped vault that may have been compromised.

claim: With multi-party approval, a group of trusted individuals can collaboratively approve access to a logically air-gapped vault from a separately created recovery account when malicious activity may compromise the primary account.

separately-created recovery account

evidence.quote: As an AWS Backup customer, you can use Multi-party approval to grant approval capabilities of some operations to a group of trusted individuals who can collaboratively approve access to a logically air-gapped vault from a separately-created recovery account in the case of suspected malicious activity that may compromise use of the primary account.

claim: There is no additional cost for multi-party approval teams with logically air-gapped vaults, but storage and cross-Region transfer charges apply.

storage and cross-region transfers charges apply

US East (N. Virginia)

evidence.quote: Multi-party approval Team resources can only be created and stored in AWS Region US East (N. Virginia).

claim: A best practice for multi-party approval is two or more AWS organizations: a primary organization that holds the logically air-gapped vaults and a secondary recovery organization where the approval team is managed.
question: Where should the multi-party approval team be managed?

values.display: Two (or more) AWS organizations
recovery organization

evidence.quote: Two (or more) AWS organizations through Organizations. One should be your primary organization where you have one or more accounts that have at least one logically air-gapped vault. The secondary organization should be your recovery organization. It is in this org where your multi-party approval team will be managed.
